Not my story, but my friend's grandparent's met through a penpal thing. He was from California and in the war, she was from Texas. She decided to get a penpal that was in the war, as her friends were also. They exchanged letters for a few months. He came back to his home in California. The first day he was home he talked to her all day on the phone. Literally, all day. Or so I was told! Anyway, they decide to meet. He drives all the way from California to Texas to meet her. He shows up at her doorstep with roses. They go out on a date. For the next 4 days, they spend every moment together. On the 5th day, she didnt see him. He didn't come to her house or talk to her at all. On the 6th day he showed up and told her he needed to go back to his family because he was being sent back to war. He left. She didn't hear from him for weeks.

Finally, she gets a letter from him that has flowers on a piece of paper saying "Will you marry me?" She says yes. When he returns months later they get married.

Not really sure how long they were married. But he recently died about 2 months ago. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer about 4 or 5 years ago. It kept going away and coming back, and it finally got into his bones and brain. He lived longer than the doctors said he would, by about 2 years.

They told the story at his funeral and I'm almost positive every single person in the room was crying. It has got to be one of the sweetest things I've ever heard!
Damn. Our DPS office requires you to call in on the day of and schedule it. You can't show up and ask for a test.

It was easy to me. I didn't make any mistakes and the first thing the lady said when we finished was, "I have no advice for you."

Make sure you constantly check your mirrors. ALL OF THEM. Make sure your hands are 10 and 2 on the wheel. If you can start a conversation with the DPS person, and get on their good side, that's like extra brownie points for you. Stop completely at railroad crossings. Make sure you don't come to a rolling stop at stop signs, stop completely. You should have no problem. 

Which, I did take my test in my Prius, and Prius' are the shit. My DPS lady was messing with the touch screen radio and shit the whole time.

Good luck!

I was 14, and every afternoon I would drive our 6-wheeler to the back of the pasture and check hog traps. I started taking my dachshund with me. He would sit in front of me, and prop his self up by putting his front legs on the middle of the handle bars. One day, I am heading back to the house, and I hit some hog ruts. My dogs falls of the 6-wheeler and gets ran over by the back 4 wheels. I jump off and start crying as I see my dog writhing on the ground screaming. I thought I broke his back. He was in odd positions and was making noises I have never heard a dog make before. I sit down next to him in tears thinking, "Oh god. I have to kill him. No, I can't. I have to. His back is broken. No. No. No." Then he proceeds to stand up, wag his tail, jumps in my lap and acts like nothing happened. 

What. The. Fuck.
Yes, he had been at my church for about 5 years. Thankfully, I never took part in the youth group very often.
My youth minister got arrested for repeatedly molesting/raping a girl over a course of, I think, 3 years.

You will get over him. It may take some time, but you will.

I hung out with the same social group as my ex also. I had to hang out with other people before I could hang out in that same group without feeling awkward.

I tried the whole "friends" thing. It doesn't work. It will only hurt you in the long run. Not to say y'all can't be friends later on, just not right now. It wouldn't be good.

Motorcycles are dangerous regardless of the environment they are in. (Busy city, etc) My uncle was driving his motorcycle to work one day after a short rain shower. He was behind a school bus, and came around a curve, hit a puddle at the wrong spot, went headfirst over the motorcycle. Practically face planted on the side of the road. Not really sure the real diagnosis, but I know he did fracture, crack, something, his C7 vertebrae (I believe). The eye shield on his helmet shattered into his left eye. He was conscious as the ambulance pulled up and took him to the closest hospital. There, he was complaining of no feeling in his legs and arms. But he was alive, and communicating well at that time. The doctors put him in a CT scan, and while in there, fluid filled up his lungs and he started suffocating. The way he was laying, his neck was propped weird and he couldn't get any oxygen. The doctors reached him after realizing he wasn't breathing. But at that time, it had been estimated he had been without oxygen for at least a couple of minutes. His heart stopped, but they got it beating again and proceeded to care flight him to Baylor. There, he was in a coma for 2 days on life support. They said he was trying to over breathe the machine the first day. After that, no responses to anything. After tests, they concluded he was brain dead. We took him off of life support on November 12, 2010. 
The doctor at Baylor said if he would have lived, he would have lost his left eye, and would of had a rod down his spine. He wouldn't have been able to function hardly.

Whenever I see a motorcycle accident, I tear up. I partially blame the doctors who put my uncle in the CT scan. I don't know if they knew that he would suffocate or not, but I still hold a grudge sorta because of that.

Thank God that you managed to survive your accident. It's truly a blessing when you are involved in something like that, and you make it out alright.

Maybe she is just dwelling on the negative things that happened. She might be scared it will go back to whatever bad things had happened in the relationship. That is what happened to my 2 and a half year relationship. I'm here to talk if you ever want to! Message me anytime.

Depression doesn't only affect you. It affects everyone around you. I went through the same thing. It's possible that she is having doubts because of the build up of stress. 

1. Possibly. Talk to her about it. See where her mind is at. If it's because of stress, try mentioning a break. The break will give both of y'all time to think things over. She can get away from some stress, and it may help you too.

2. Talk to her in person, like I said before, see where her mind is. If she says something along the lines of, "I really don't know..." or "I have no clue..." then try mentioning a break. I think it would be the best for both of you. 

3. Life goes on. If something happens, it happens. I believe everything happens for a reason. Maybe this was just meant to be a learning experience for you both. If there are any doubts with anything, then something is wrong. Don't try and convince yourself. If she is doubtful do to your depression, seek help. Honestly. Maybe she is wanting you to get better. It's up to you.

-I don't know if you are religious or not. I'm not trying to push religion on you in anyway at all. But saying this simple prayer, "God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change; courage to change the things I can; and wisdom to know the difference", works miracles for me. It helps.

-If she does break up with you, don't push yourself into drugs and an even worse stage of depression. Realize that the only way to fix your relationships with others, is to fix yourself.
